dataset: AI Advisor Questionnaire: Documented Survey Responses

notes: Response counts vary because some questions were optional.
For select-all-that-apply questions, percentages do not sum to 100%.
Percentages describe surveyed respondents and should not be generalized to all Illinois Tech students.

respondent_profile.major_note: Majors were entered as free text with inconsistent spellings and abbreviations; normalization is needed before reliable major-level comparisons.

findings.interpretation: Reported advising satisfaction was moderate, and relatively few respondents rated access to advising as easy or very easy.
Career planning, graduation planning, and course selection were the most frequently selected difficulties within this sample.
Nearly two-thirds of respondents reported sometimes or often being unsure which courses to take next semester.
Respondents most often reported searching the university website or asking other students when immediate advisor help was unavailable.
Most respondents rated the potential importance of, and their comfort with, AI advising highly.
Course planning, graduation progress tracking, and career recommendations received the most selections in the feature question.

responses.situation: Comfortable using AI for most advising tasks

findings.interpretation: Most selected a human advisor for personal or sensitive situations; some also selected high-impact academic and registration decisions.

responses.data: Would not want any personal information accessed

findings.interpretation: Many respondents indicated willingness to share student information for personalization, but privacy concern varied and some reported the highest concern rating.
Source explanations were rated important by most respondents.

qualitative_themes: Faster and easier access to advising help
Clearer information and advice before advisor meetings
Earlier and more detailed career guidance
AI working alongside human academic advisors
Requests for clearer wording of what academic advising means in the survey
findings.interpretation: These themes reflect a small, optional set of comments and were not counted as prevalence estimates.

research_limitations: Thirty-five submissions comprise a small, nonrepresentative convenience sample; recruitment method and response rate were not documented in the survey PDF.
Fourth-year students (42.9%) and graduate students (20.0%) are prominent in the sample, so results should not automatically represent other class years.
Free-text major labels contain duplicates/variants and need normalization before major-by-major analysis.
Only 12 respondents answered the open-ended improvement question.
Some survey questions were optional, and multi-select percentages cannot be added together.
Stated perceived usefulness or comfort does not prove actual usage, safety, or technical feasibility.
next_research_actions: Discuss reported career-planning, graduation-planning, and course-selection difficulties with advisors across departments.
Ask advisors which frequent student questions can be answered reliably from official sources and which require human judgment.
Investigate exceptions, outdated data, catalog-year variation, and escalation rules.
Use interviews to corroborate or challenge student survey findings before proposing development priorities.

privacy.contents: Aggregated questionnaire results and analyst interpretations only; no student-identifying information.
privacy.public_repo_note: Confirm the public release of aggregated research findings is allowed by your project/instructor before committing.
